evals.name: youtube-mrbeast-opening
evals.prompt: i want to steal MrBeast's pacing for my own channel. dissect the first 3 minutes of this and give me a template i can actually follow: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0e3GPea1Tyg
evals.expected_output: A blueprint .md covering only the opening ~3 minutes: frame-by-frame hook, beat sheet with timestamps, cut rate and words per minute, retention devices, a fill-in script template and ready-to-use prompts, with short quotes only.
assertions: A blueprint Markdown file (100+ lines) was produced
Breaks down the opening seconds in detail (4+ table rows timed within the first 12 s)
Has a beat sheet with 4+ timestamped beats
States the cut rate as a number (cuts per minute or average shot length)
States the speaking pace in words per minute, or notes that there's no speech
Describes the sound design (music and/or sound effects)
Includes a fill-in-the-blanks template (5+ placeholders)
Includes ready-to-paste generation prompts (in code blocks)
Keeps quotes from the video short (no quoted passage over 25 words)
Doesn't reproduce the transcript (under 30% of its 6-word runs appear)
Separates the creator's personal signature from the reusable format
Analyses the voice beyond pace (4+ of pitch, pauses, emphasis, energy/tone, endings, accent)
Gives voice direction a narrator or text-to-speech tool could use
Specifies the on-screen text / caption style concretely (font, colour and position)
Covers only the requested opening ~3 minutes (no table timestamp past 3:15)
Uses YouTube audience data (views, likes, comments or most-replayed moments)
Writes data/timeline.json and measured.md, and the blueprint has the measured shot table with start and end frames
Lists the transition into each shot with its type and length in frames (plate 5)
Gives camera or element moves as numbers (travel %, scale, easing), not only names
Has a type spec with cap heights in px at 1080p and a phone minimum
Ships the frame sheets: hook, one frame per shot, transition strips and the timeline sheet
Assembles cleanly: dissect.py assemble reports no CONTRADICTION warnings

evals.name: x-launch-film-rebuild-and-check
evals.prompt: i want to make a launch film for my fintech app exactly in the style of this one, give me something claude code can actually build from: https://x.com/solana/status/2107994265104339166 . then tell me how close this render is: ~/Downloads/refs-pack/ab3008/norra-south.mp4
evals.expected_output: A v2 blueprint (<slug>.blueprint.md) plus <slug>.timeline.json with frame-exact shots (1199 frames at 30 fps), the karaoke hold-line captions, the blur swap at f598, three benefit words, brand placeholders and a recipe prompt; then a check report scoring the render (about 80/100) with frame-level fixes.
assertions: A blueprint Markdown file (300+ lines) and a <slug>.timeline.json were produced
The shot table gives frames at 30 fps and the film's 1199-frame length (not 1200)
Describes the hold-line captions as word-by-word lit (karaoke) text that scrolls
Names three benefit words, not two, with the swap to the third around 32.3 s
Treats the transition at frame 598 as a blur swap of the text (not a camera whip), or flags the label as low confidence
Gives the big scale-down on the first benefit word as keyframes or start and end frames with easing
Says the reference's section levels are RMS, not LUFS, and gives a loudness target per platform
Recipe prompt uses {{PRODUCT}}, {{BRAND_FONT}}, {{BRAND_BG}}, {{BRAND_ACCENTS}}, {{LOGO}}, {{CTA_URL}} and no reference hex colours
Does not tell the builder to follow the reference's colour while also telling them not to use its palette
Runs dissect.py check on the render and reports a score out of 100 with fixes that name frames
